messages:
Maya: Quick follow-up on the canonical service identity RFC — my proposal: every span/resource must resolve to a canonical triple: service.namespace, service.name, service.instance_id. Use that triple as the source-of-truth for cost attribution and routing.

Luca: Quick q: how do we populate that for edge auto-instrumented workloads where libs only expose hostnames?

Maya: Two options: 1) a short propagated header from the edge (X-Redwood-Service) that contains a compact mapping id, 2) fallback to resolver that maps host -> service.* using a service-registry lookup. Prefer 1 for correctness, 2 as defensive fallback.

Priya: Concern: if we attach instance_id on every span we blow up cardinality. Can we keep instance_id at the resource level and avoid repeating it on every event?

Maya: Yes — resource-level attributes are fine. Ingest should hydrate resource attrs into the span during enrichment for downstream joins, but we don't need instance_id copied into every raw span field that increases index cardinality.

Sam: Implementation sketch: edge proxy adds header: `X-Redwood-Service: svc://payments/checkout#checkout-123` (compact). Ingest enrich: parse header into resource attrs. We'll store canonical ids as integers in the proto to keep size down.

Maya: Example minimal enrichment pseudo-snippet:
```
resource.attrs = {
  "service.namespace": "payments",
  "service.name": "checkout",
  "service.instance_id": "checkout-123",
  // optional: tenant if available
  "redwood.tenant_id": "org-42"
}
// spans do not duplicate instance_id unless necessary
span.attrs = { "http.method":"POST", "http.status_code":"200" }
```

Priya: That helps. Still need a policy for when instance_id is omitted: resolver should return `service.unknown-instance` or use `service.name@host` fallback to avoid nulls.

Luca: For backwards compatibility, we should accept both older `rbw-service` header and new `X-Redwood-Service` for a year. Also we need a migration table: old tag -> canonical triple.

Maya: Agreed. Rollout plan I propose: phase 0: canary accept header + passive mapping; phase 1: enrich and surface in console; phase 2: make mapping authoritative for cost attribution; phase 3: enforce at agent/edge level and remove legacy tags.

Sam: Metrics to gate rollout: ingest CPU delta < 8%, tail latency increase < 5ms, ingestion storage delta < 2% at canary scale. We should create a tag-explosion test harness that simulates 100k unique instance_ids.

infra-bot: runbook created: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/service-id-rollout (permission: eng-platform). Canary cluster: obs-canary-3.

Priya: Backfill question — how do we join historical spans to new canonical ids for cost reports? My suggestion: run a daily join job that maps legacy tags -> canonical id using the registry and create a compressed mapping blob we can query at report time. Avoid rewriting raw events.

Luca: +1. Also add an epoch-based mapping header for deterministic joins (mapping_v1 = timestamp).

Maya: Action items: Sam to own canary runs and harness (due 1 week), Priya to draft backfill job spec (due 1 week), Luca to update edge proxy header PR (due 3 days). I'll file the follow-up RFC with rollout phases & gating metrics. :thumbsup:

Sam: I'll seed the harness tomorrow and post results in this thread.

Maya: Thanks all — we'll sync in the eng-platform weekly if anything blocks.

Luca: leaving a note: consider privacy constraints for tenant propagation (PII). If tenant_id is present, ensure KMS tagging controls.

Maya: Good call. We'll add a privacy checklist to the RFC.
